review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for repeated non-trivial proofs and checked the related uses of the private lemmas. I did not run Lean, so none of the proposed replacements has been compiled. One uncertainty concerns the module system. The public `@[expose]` defs `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv` and `baseChangeTowerIso` would reference the private lemmas `globalSectionsBaseChange_isPushout` and `baseChangeTower_isPullback`. The reference sits only in proof terms, so it may be fine as it is. If it is not, the fix is to drop `private` from those two lemmas. The two `*_eq_oldConstruction` `rfl` lemmas show the author already knows the lemma-based and inlined versions are definitionally equal.

findings.excerpt:
let H : IsPullback (pullback.fst p s) (pullback.snd p s) p s :=
      IsPullback.of_hasPullback p s
findings.problem: The roughly 40-line proof that the global-section square is a pushout appears twice, line for line. The first copy is `globalSectionsBaseChange_isPushout` (lines 74-112). The second is the `let h : IsPushout ...` block inside `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv`. Both run the same steps: flatness of `Spec K → Spec k` from a field, the `pushoutSection` isomorphism for the qcqs flat base change, `isIso_pushoutSection_iff`, then `of_iso` with `ΓSpecIso`. Later declarations (`_tmul_one`, `_one_tmul`) call the lemma, while the definition they are about re-inlines it. `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv_eq_oldConstruction` is proved by `rfl`, so the two are already definitionally equal. Any fix to the pushout argument has to be made twice, and the definition is about 40 lines longer than it needs to be.
findings.proposed_change: In `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv`, replace the whole `let h : IsPushout ... := by ...` block with `let h := globalSectionsBaseChange_isPushout k K p`. Both places have the same hypotheses `[CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]` and the same `letI := p.globalSectionsAlgebra k`, so no new hypotheses are needed. Then delete `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv_eq_oldConstruction`, since the two sides coincide syntactically. If an `@[expose]` def cannot mention a private lemma, drop `private` from `globalSectionsBaseChange_isPushout`.
findings.benefit: The pushout argument exists once, so a reader sees what the equivalence rests on without wading through a duplicate. The definition shrinks to the tensor-product identification and the `commutes'` field. All three uses (`Equiv`, `_tmul_one`, `_one_tmul`) share one source of `h`. The `rfl` lemma, which only exists to compare the two copies, goes away.

findings.problem: `baseChangeTower_isPullback` (lines 387-410) proves the composite pullback square. It pastes the two pullbacks and rewrites with `sL ≫ sK = Spec.map (algebraMap k L)`, using `IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply`. `baseChangeTowerIso` then repeats the same proof as a `show ... from by` term, restating the whole statement of the square. Later lemmas use the private lemma, and `baseChangeTowerIso_eq_oldConstruction` is again proved by `rfl`. The result is two copies of the proof and a duplicated, very long type ascription.
findings.proposed_change: Define `baseChangeTowerIso` as `(baseChangeTower_isPullback k K L p).isoIsPullback X (Spec (.of L)) (IsPullback.of_hasPullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))))`. This is exactly the right-hand side of `baseChangeTowerIso_eq_oldConstruction`. Delete the `show ... from by ...` block and that `rfl` lemma. If the module system objects, make `baseChangeTower_isPullback` non-private.
findings.benefit: The definition drops from about 35 lines to a few. The one proof of the pasted square is shared by the definition and by `baseChangeTowerIso_hom_fst` and `baseChangeTowerIso_hom_snd`. The restated square type is no longer written out twice.

findings.problem: These two definitions (identity at 329-352, tower at 523-550) build the same thing from an isomorphism of schemes. They take `e.inv.app ⊤` as a ring equivalence via `asIso ... commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv`. They then prove `commutes'` by the same chain: unfold to `appTop.hom.comp (ΓSpecIso).inv.hom`, `congr 1`, then `RingHom.comp_assoc`, `← CommRingCat.hom_comp`, `← Hom.comp_appTop`, and the lemma `e.inv ≫ snd = ...`. Each also repeats the `letI : IsIso e.inv` and `IsIso (e.inv.app ⊤)` boilerplate. The only mathematical input is `e.inv ≫ a = b` for the structure maps to `Spec K`, so the scaffolding is copied twice.
findings.proposed_change: Add one helper. For `a : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K)`, `b : Z ⟶ Spec (.of K)`, `f : Z ⟶ Y` with `[IsIso f]` and `h : f ≫ a = b`, define `Hom.globalSectionsAlgEquivOfComp` with type `letI := a.globalSectionsAlgebra K; letI := b.globalSectionsAlgebra K; Γ(Y, ⊤) ≃ₐ[K] Γ(Z, ⊤)`. Its `toRingEquiv` is `(asIso (f.app ⊤)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv`, and `commutes'` is the shared `rw` chain using `h`. `baseChangeGlobalSectionsAlgebra k K p` is defeq to `(pullback.snd p _).globalSectionsAlgebra K`, as the definitions at lines 57-61 and 50-52 show. The two public equivalences then become `helper (baseChangeIdentityIso k p).inv (baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_snd k p)` and `helper (baseChangeTowerIso k K L p).inv (baseChangeTowerIso_inv_snd k K L p)`. The `_apply` lemmas stay `rfl`.
findings.benefit: The compatibility-with-structure-map argument is written once. Both equivalences shrink to one line plus their already-proved `inv_snd` lemmas. Any later transport along an isomorphism of schemes over `Spec K` can reuse the helper.
